properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 3/02/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in German Township, Fayette county. 102.4(b)5 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – The E & S Plan did not contain the required drawings and narrative.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 3/02/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)5 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – The E & S Plan did not contain the required drawings and narrative.
Violation ID: 8266630
Permit API: 051-21886
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/02/2026
Comments: On March 2, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4128962.The Department and the Operator entered into a COA for this site in March 7, 2019.E and S Plans on-site are not updated as discussed in IR 4128962. The Department requested new E and S phase and Restoration phase drawings added to the plan set to include the rough delineation of the wetland. The Department also requested adding a wetland seed mix to the delineated wetland, which has also not been added to the plan set. CFS near the access road entrance and stockpile along the access road appear to have been impacted by truck traffic. The Department recommends the operator maintain the CFS and ensure it is installed properly. No E and S issues are observed at this time.Orange construction fence has been installed surrounding the flowing surface water from the wetland. Operator has added compost chinking to the existing CFS on-site. No additional CFS appears to have been installed at this time. CFS surrounding the site and wetland appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. No E and S issues are observed at this time. What appears to be absorbent pads are observed within the flowing water on site (Photos 14-16, 22). Specific conductivity was recorded for background and within the area of the absorbent pads to assess for possible spill. The Department did not observe elevated specific conductivity readings or a sheen in the water near the pads. However the Department requests a response with information on why the absorbent pads are located within the water on site.The pipe identified in IRs 4125575 and 4128962 appears to have been removed as described by the operator in the NOV response. As requested in IR 4128962, the Department requests a written response to include any findings regarding the pipe, including the size of the pipe, use, and if it was connected to additional equipment. Violations remain outstanding at this time. The Department requests the plan set be updated and a written response be received by the Department by March 16, 2026.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/08/2024 to EQT ARO LLC in Burnside Township, Centre county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/08/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8174745
Permit API: 027-21517
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Burnside Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/08/2024
Comments: Rick Hall of EQT reported a spill to the Department on 2/6/24. Mr. Hall reported that during the plugging operation of well 027-21517 on 1/23/24, they were flowing the well to a gas buster and a spray/mist came out of the gas buster. It was estimated as 3 gallons at the time so it wasnt reported to DEP at that time. They scraped it up.On 2/5/24, they discovered that since 1/23/24, things have warmed up, there has been melting, and they discovered water that had elevated conductivity. They scraped some additional material and found that the spill is deeper than originally expected. I conducted an incident inspection on 2/8/24 with Bo Hampson of EQT. According to Mr. Hampson, all impacted materials have been scraped up and removed from the site. Evaluated readings were found under the gas buster so for now, the operator has installed additional containment on both sides of the gas buster. Once the plugging operation is ceased, they will remove the gas buster, containment, and further investigate the impacted area. I conducted field screenings on various spots near the gas buster and throughout the well pad using a Hanna Gro Line Soil probe. Readings ranged from 0.01 mS/cm to 0.62 mS/cm near the gas buster. I was unable to screen right next to the gas buster due to additional containment. Please contact notify me when the gas buster will be removed from the site so I can conduct additional screenings. The Department recommends that the operator pursue Act 2 due to the unknown volume. Violations have been cited.

Violation ID: 8179675
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2024
Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Comments: On 06/15/2026, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the MELENYZER F77 in Fallowfield Township, Washington County. The following was observed during inspection:-A well tag was observed on the pump jack. I recommend a well tag placed on the well head (Photo 1).- The well and operator's information were displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h) (Photo 2). -I observed corrosion on the well head and pump jack. Elevated Conductivity readings taken in the area of the release were 18.62 mS/cm and 9.31 mS/cm near the surface and Over range readings approximately 8 inches in the ground. The conductivity readings taken are elevated above the background reading of 533 uS/cm. It appears the spill is greater than 5 gallons (Photo 3-14).-Some corrosion was observed on the production equipment and production tank (Photo 15-17).Field Scout Conductivity Probe was calibrated on 06/15/2026 before inspection was conducted. The operator was contacted on 06/15/2026 about Departments observationsDetermination: Violations are being issued for spill: 78.57(a), 78.54, 91.34(a), SWMA 301.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/13/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/13/2022

Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/13/2022
Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources was onsite and said STL Resources plans to continue the investigation of the extent of this spill area once the containment has been removed. The top layer of soil has been removed in this area adjacent to the containment in about a 10 ft. x 10 ft. area. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of thewell pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being hauled off site or pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in the northwest stormwater vault. In the southwest stormwater vault, the conductivity of the water was 1,939 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.3 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 23.7 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 71.9 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 133.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32 uS/cm. Seep 3 was not able to be screened with the conductivity meter due to the lack of water at the seep. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 90.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.6 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, 3445592, and 3467217.

Comments: Arrived onsite for a routine inspection.There were 2 wells, 2 GPUs, 2 sand separators, 1 compressor, and 1 produced water tank onsite.The site was vegetated and appeared stable. Code 78a.56(a)This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued.I departed at 1125 hours.

Comments: Inspection of Chesapeake's "Jads" Marcellus well site.Aaron Stredny (Chesapeake) called the DEP on Friday August 19, 2022 to report an estimated 50 gallon spill of diesel fuel. The spill happened when a fuel tank fell off a forklift. A vac truck already on site removed the standing liquid fuel, they also used absorbent pads on the fuel.I spoke with Danny Lambert (Company Man) on site. He showed me where the fuel spill occurred, which is now a water puddle. I did not see any sheen or evidence of residual fuel on the pad. A MiniRae 3000 photoionization detector with a 10.6 eV bulb returned 0.0 ppm readings from the spill area, indicating absence of volatiles emitting from that area. Creston Environmental is arriving tomorrow to delineate the impacted pad area for excavation and sampling. Nabors' X25 rig is installing production casing in the the 3rd of 6 Marcellus wells here today. Tomorrow they start drilling the 4th well. They drill on water/bentonite until ~7,000' depth, then switch to diesel based mud for "kickoff" into the horizontal section. Lambert expects to finish drilling here in October 2022.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.I did not see any Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls in place.Pooled on the pad surface in 5 separate areas has electrical conductivity of 0.46-0.67 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. Air temp 79FJLP

Comments: On April 25, 2024, routine inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources Inc well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on April 1, 2016.The following was observed:Well 10H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 1 and 2). A small amount of grease was observed on the well pad surface below the well head (see photo 3). There are five other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 4). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 5). Additional secondary containment that appeared to be severely deteriorated was observed next to the production tanks (see photo 6). This appears to be used for pump trucks that empty the production tanks. The ERP and PPC plan were onsite (see photos 7 and 8). Deep accelerated erosion rills were observed in multiple portions of the access road, with one of them appearing to empty into a storm culvert (see photos 11-15). The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that any grease or other fluids used during routine maintenance that fall onto the well pad surface are immediately removed. The Department also recommends that deteriorated secondary containments and other onsite equipment are replaced to mitigate the risk of a spill from occurring on site. Finally, the Department recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that contain regulated substances are equipped with secondary containments to mitigate the risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.Violations are being issued against the severely eroded access road.

The completion of plugging for this well reportedly occurred 12/27/2023, therefore the Operator is in compliance with the COA issued on 12/16/2021. The Operator has 9 months from plugging to complete a restoration of the former well site. Discussion between MAWC and the Operator(Stone Ridge Energy) had taken place onsite about restoration efforts of the site during this inspection. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at this time. Violations are outstanding, but are listed as new in this inspection report due to an app error.

Comments: On August 6, 2024, the Department of Oil and Gas inspector, Cody Murray, conducted an onsite inspection of the HERBERT C SMITH 193C (Permit # 021-20851), operated by VESSELS COAL GAS INC.. • There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere to be found. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/28/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Cahill" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP yesterday (August 27, 2025) to report they discovered an underground flow line leaked an unknown quantity of produced liquid.I spoke with Mike Deming (Expand) on site during this inspection who explained their Forward Looking Infrared (FLIR) camera technician discovered natural gas emitting from the pad surface on Friday August 22, 2025 during a quarterly inspection. On Monday August 25, 2025 Expand pressurized all 3 Marcellus wells with natural gas. The 2H Marcellus well lost approximately 500 psi over 20 minutes, indicating the leak. On Wednesday August 27, 2025 they pressurized the 2H well with air to locate the production line leaks more accurately. Expand checked the fill slope for signs of seepage, and did not see any liquid or stressed vegetation.I spoke with Andy Senefelder (Crescent Environmental, P.G.) on site who explained that yesterday an excavator dug a ~3' deep x ~90' long trench above the production lines. Then they hand dug 9 test pits ("potholes") in the pea gravel surrounding the production line to find the extent of the leaks. Liquid in the potholes returned electrical conductivity (EC) readings of 23-106 mS/cm. Crescent tested the pad material removed for the trench which returned EC readings of 0.05-0.45 mS/cm, indicating the material above the line is not impacted. So far, a vac truck has removed approximately 2 barrels of liquid from sumps in the trench. Demming calculated the approximate maximum amount of liquid released is 21.5 barrels.Expand removed the 2 sections of 4" diameter line that leaked, and are testing the metal to determine a cause of the pinholes in it. They plan to replace all of the production lines between the wells and the GPUs with above ground pipe.After the old lines are removed, Crescent plans to sample in compliance with Act 2 Cleanup standards.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion orsedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Runoff water flows to basins on the east and south ends of the site.Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles on the east end of the pad surface has EC of 0.30-0.55 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5. I did not see any other puddles on the pad.Violations for the production liquid release are cited to the 2H well permit.Air temp 54FJLP

Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 10/31/2025
Comments: On 10/31/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 43 degrees, overcast and lightly sprinkling when I arrived on location. Rainfall has impacted the region in the last 24 hours.Upon my arrival, I first inspected the original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well. A plugged well monument is installed above the well with a plugged date of 3/24/2025. All servicing equipment has been removed from this pad. The pad has not been reclaimed and the temporary access road and temporary bridges remain installed.When I arrive on the active site, I met Seneca's Wes Sammins who described current operations as follows: Patterson drilling rig #805 has been mobilized to the site to drill an additional eight wells at the site. The rig was towered up over the 70HU, and had started drilling surface on 10/28/2025. The rig was currently drilling the intermediate at 1568 feet with the intermediate going to 3350 feet, then to total depth at 23514 feet. Wes expects to drill one more well that is in the process of being repermitted. Six wells have been completed this run. Secondary containment has been installed for drilling operations. 12 frac tanks, diesel tanks, and chemicals were staged in secondary containment around the drilling rig. Drill cuttings were being collected, solidified and temporarily stored in 6 dumpsters. 28 frac tanks remain staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. There are five newly drilled and completed wells on site that were staged for production. Sand separators were attached to the wells, the sand separators all connected to two frac tanks. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Liquid in a 5' x 40' puddle on the unprotected ground north of the GPUs field tested at 1875 mS conductance. I discussed this with Wes who arranged for the liquid to be removed.A 40 foot channel of water immediately east of the central outfall from the pad field tested at 2030 uS conductance. Liquid draining from the north center outfall into the basin field tested at 2020 uS conductance. Liquid in the sediment basin next to the northeast overflow field tested at 1380 uS conductance. Liquid was observed flowing through the northern most compost filter sock and leaving the site; the liquid field tested at 1201 uS conductance. Liquid flowing past the LOD field tested at 1409 uS conductance.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's OMR 02-188 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 11/30/2022 at 0920 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with an overcast, light rain and moderate winds. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced water reported by the operator. Complaint tracking system (CTS) ID #368537 is tied to this release within CTSOn 11/29/2022 Repsol reported a 42 gallon release of produced water to the ground surface at the OMR 02-188 well site after a produced water flow-line was cut during the teardown process. Some produced water was initially pumped out of the line but not all was recovered prior to the cut of the flow-line. The produced water was then released to the ground in numerous areas along the flow-line. The impacted areas were then covered with tarps to help keep the areas free from the projected rain prior to excavation/remediation.During today's inspection, the impacted areas remained covered with tarps and a secondary containment liner to help prevent rain from spreading the release. Water present in the rock-lined channel located below the release area was field measured for electrical conductivity between 200us/cm to 380us/cm. Pad material and soils around the impacted areas covered by tarps were field measured for electrical conductivity between 0.1mS/cm and 0.3mS/cm. No evidence suggests that the release was able to reach the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls.The operator was awaiting an 811 call approval and for the environmental consultant to arrive in order to begin remediation. Current estimations put an excavation start time at 1300 hours on 11/30/2022. Discussion with an operator representative onsite places the release estimate at ~42 gallons, or one barrel, but it is not exactly known. Current rainfall would have a chance to commingle with the release prior to total recovery. Photos of the initial release discovery were provided to me via email. The operator explained that Act 2 sampling was planned to be conducted.Based on the reported release of 42 gallons of produced water to the ground, violations of the following are cited against API #117-22132 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)I departed the site at 1020 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/05/2024 to EQT CHAP LLC in Washington Township, Fayette county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT CHAP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/05/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8197141
Permit API: 051-24309
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/05/2024
Comments: On August 5 2024, the Department responded to an incident occuring in Fayette County, Washington Township. On August 5 2024 at 11:25am, the Department received a report that around 11:00am a truck on loading produced water from the production tanks had equipment malfunction resulting in an estimate of over 5 gallons spilling onto the ground. An EQT representative stated that it spilled on the ground but did not get into the waterways of commonwealth. At the time of this inspection, Act 9 Sign was present but faded. The Department recommends that the Operator update the Act 9 Sign as appropriate to ensure compliance with 78a55. At the time of this inspection, a third party representative of EQT (Specialized Professional Services Inc.) was completing clean up of the affected area. Equipment was present. Excavation was actively occurring during this inspection. The affected area was near the off loading and on/off loading area of the production tanks. According to a SPSI representative, a truck was unloading production fluid from the production tanks and had a failure at the connection, which caused production fluid to spill near the on/off loading site and visually extended down the side of the access road roughly 50ft. The SPSI representative stated that roughly 10 to 15 gallons spilled. Soil conductivity readings as well as a background soil conductivity reading was taken. The background soil conductivity reading was 0.1145mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken within the affected area were 0.458mS, 0.0031mS, and 0.0979mS. One reading in the visually affected area was elevated above the background reading of 0.1145mS. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the fluid release in accordance with 78a.66. The Department also requests the Operator evaluate the release that has occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred, to be provided in the requested NOV Response. The Department also requests waste manifests upon proper disposal of wastes generated from the spill remediation.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued at this time.

Comments: On 04/02/2026, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the X-Man Well Site. The Emergency Response Plan was on site (Photo 1).The access road was in generally good condition. I observed accelerated erosion near the top of the road. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: 78a59b(g) - WELL DEVELOPMENT IMPOUNDMENTS - Operator failed to properly restore the impoundment within 9 months of completion of hydraulic fracturing of the last well serviced by the impoundment.
Violation ID: 948149
Permit API: 047-24636
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 10/13/2011. There is a second active well (047-24587) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 9/16/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0024 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-half of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. A well development impoundment (Impoundment # 6) is located approximately 3800’ northeast of the HM2 well site (41.53798¿ / -78.70414¿). This impoundment is covered by the same ESCGP that encompasses the HM2 well site. The impoundment has not yet been restored, and greater than nine months have passed since the last well was serviced by this impoundment. The Department does not have record showing that this well development impoundment has been registered, as is required by Chapter 78a.59b(b). The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. There are isolated areas of scouring that should be addressed in an effort to avoid potential E&S issues in the future. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to Bear Creek and several unnamed tributaries. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

Violation ID: 8210425

Inspection Date: 12/09/2024
Comments: On 12/09/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1200 hours, weather was 40F and raining. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Stimulation activities for the two recently drilled wells are ongoing, equipment is located onsite to support these activities (photos #2-5). See inspection report #3878285 for more details. The accessible area excavated due to the release noted in inspection report #3878285 has been backfilled and fluids in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~701-741us/cm (photo #6). The remaining impacted area from this release will be excavated and backfilled upon removal of the rig matting covering that area. DEP Environmental Cleanups and Brownsfield personnel were onsite prior to my arrival to follow up on the release detailed in inspection report #3878285 and noted concerns regarding a diesel sheen observed on portions of the pad surface.The source of the diesel was investigated by Greylock and it was determined that a maintenance truck located onsite had released an undetermined amount of diesel, the truck was removed from the site and staff were working on removing diesel from the pad surface at the time of this inspection (photos #7-10). Fluid was observed overtopping from the secondary containment structure of the produced fluids offload area onsite (photos #11 and 12). This fluid was combining with rainwater and the diesel sheen on the pad surface and moving into the pad's drainage system which transports water from the pad surface to the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control. Fluids on the pad surface near the offload containment structure field measured for EC at ~10.32-15.93mS/cm; personnel from Penn E and R measured a similar result of 11.10mS/cm (photos #14-16).The pad drainage system services the site's infiltration basin via two pipes which move fluids from their respective half of the pad (photo #17). One pipe is located closer to the produced fluids offload area and the other is located near the wellheads. Fluid with a diesel sheen was observed discharging into the infiltration basin from the pipe near the offload area; this fluid field measured for EC at ~1.35mS/cm and the soil near this area field measured for EC at ~1.20mS/cm (photos #18-20). Fluid discharging from the pipe near the wellheads field measured for EC at ~0.908mS/cm (photo #21). Vacuum trucks were dispatched to remove fluids from the secondary containment structures and the pad surface in response to the release (photo #22). Personnel were also working to install sump pumps and shut in the drainage pipes to prevent any further discharge into the basin.I followed up with Greylock and they informed me that the drains discharging into the basin were shut in at 1400 hours and they were recovering fluids from basin with a vacuum truck.The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to prevent fluids from reaching PCSM controls until all contaminated fluids and soils are recovered.-Removing fluids from containment structures as it accumulates.-Following Act 2 to remediate the infiltration basin, diesel spill, and produced fluids containment release.Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #105-21962:-25 PA 78a64a(f) due to the observation of produced fluids overtopping from a secondary containment structure and being conveyed into the sites PCSM controls. -35 P.S. 691.401 due to the release of produced fluids and diesel discharging into the site's PCSM controls.The violations cited in inspection report #3878285 remain outstanding due to the remediation requirements outlined in 25 PA 78a.66(c)(2)(i) having not yet been met.I departed the site at 1345.
